sentences.text:
PROSECUTION STORY:
4. The applicant is stated to have enticed away the daughter of the informant, when she had gone to temple, and had administered certain noxious material, thereby rendering her unconscious.
Thereafter, he committed rape with her and also video-recorded the said act.
5.
The applicant is stated to have threatened her to make the said video viral on social media and kept on establishing the said relationship subsequently also.

6. On 21.5.2024 at about 7.30 pm, the applicant is stated to have called the daughter of the informant, who, thereupon, had taken away ornaments worth Rs. 2.5 lakhs and cash of Rs. 7,000/-
from her house and had given them to the applicant.

7. After finding the said ornaments missing, the informant is stated to have questioned the victim,
who, as such, revealed the whole incident to him.
ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF THE APPLICANT:
8. The applicant is absolutely innocent and has been falsely implicated in the present case with a view to cause unnecessary harassment and to victimize him.
He has nothing to do with the said offence.
9. The FIR is delayed by two days as far as the last incident is concerned.
It is further delayed by a month since the incident of rape.

There is no recovery of any ornament or cash or any video,
whatsoever.
10. The victim by her looks, seems to be major.
As per the ossification test report, her age has come out to be 18 years.
As per the High School Certificate, her age is marginally less than 18 years.
11. The informant had earlier on instituted an FIR against unknown person on 7.5.2024 regarding the missing of the same girl since 6.5.2024.

The said girl was recovered by the police and was handed over to the informant by C.W.C.
12.
Several other submissions have been made on behalf of the applicant to demonstrate the falsity of the allegations made against him.
The circumstances which, as per counsel, led to the false implication of the applicant have also been touched upon at length.
13. There is no criminal history of the applicant.
The applicant is languishing in jail since 3.7.2024.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he will not misuse the liberty of bail.

ARGUMENTS ON BEHALF OF INFORMANT/STATE:

sentences.text: The bail application has been opposed but the fact that there is no criminal history of the applicant has not been disputed.

CONCLUSION:
15. The well-known principle of "Presumption of Innocence Unless Proven Guilty," gives rise to the concept of bail as a rule and imprisonment as an exception.

16. A person's right to life and liberty, guaranteed by Article 21 of the Indian Constitution, cannot be taken away simply because the person is accused of committing an offence until the guilt is established beyond a reasonable doubt.

Article 21 of the Indian Constitution states that no one's life or personal liberty may be taken away unless the procedure established by law is followed, and the procedure must be just and reasonable.

The said principle has been recapitulated by the Supreme Court in Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690.
17.

entities.text: Satender Kumar Antil Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation and Ors., 2022 INSC 690
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Reiterating the aforesaid view the Supreme Court in the case of Manish Sisodia Vs. Directorate of Enforcement 2024 INSC 595 has again emphasised that the very well-settled principle of law that bail is not to be withheld as a punishment is not to be forgotten.

entities.text: Manish Sisodia Vs. Directorate of Enforcement 2024 INSC 595
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is high time that the Courts should recognize the principle that ?bail is a rule and jail is an exception?.
18. Learned State Law Officer could not bring forth any exceptional circumstances which would warrant denial of bail to the applicant.
19. It is settled principle of law that the object of bail is to secure the attendance of the accused at the trial.

No material particulars or circumstances suggestive of the applicant fleeing from justice or thwarting the course of justice or creating other troubles in the shape of repeating offences or intimidating witnesses and the like have been shown by learned State Law Officer.

20. Considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for the parties, the evidence on record, and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case,
the Court is of the view that the applicant has made out a case for bail.
The bail application is allowed.

21. Let the applicant- Abhay Pratap Singh involved in aforementioned case crime number be released on bail on furnishing a personal bond and two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the court concerned subject to following conditions.
(i) The applicant shall not tamper with evidence.
(ii) The applicant shall remain present, in person, before the Trial Court on dates fixed for (1) opening of the case, (2) framing of charge and (3) recording of statement under Section 313 Cr.P.C.

If in the opinion of the Trial Court absence of the applicant is deliberate or without sufficient cause, then it shall be open for the Trial Court to treat such default as abuse of liberty of bail and proceed against him in accordance Abhay Pratap Singh vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/108768788/
3 with law.

sentences.text: 22. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, it shall be a ground for cancellation of bail.
Identity, status and residence proof of the applicant and sureties be verified by the court concerned before the bonds are accepted.

23. It is made clear that observations made in granting bail to the applicant shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
